cv: Frontend engineer with 6 years of experience, based in London
Led a team of four building a payments dashboard in React and TypeScript
Cut page load time by 40 percent on the checkout flow
Wrote the Node.js API behind a mobile banking app
Moved a 200-screen app from JavaScript to TypeScript with no downtime
Ran the weekly on-call rota for a team of five engineers
BSc Computer Science, University of Leeds, 2016
Skills: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Jest, Cypress

goal.title: Frontend engineer
goal.ask: I'm looking for a frontend engineer job, in London or remote in the UK, paying at least £50,000 a year. Here is my CV:

postings.label: fit

Location: London, two days a week in the office.
Salary: £55,000 to £65,000 a year.
You will own the speed of our checkout app, working in React and TypeScript. You will also help move our APIs to GraphQL, which most of the team is new to.

/company/kestrel: Kestrel Payments processes card payments for 4,000 small shops across the UK.
Kestrel was founded in 2019 and has 120 people, 35 of them engineers.
Our checkout widget loads in under 800 ms for most shoppers, and we are cutting that to 500 ms this year.
/company/kestrel/engineering: Engineers work in squads of five, and each squad takes a week on call every six weeks.
The web app is React and TypeScript, and the team is moving its REST endpoints to GraphQL during 2027.
Every change ships behind a feature flag and is released daily.
